clue.text: A shack in a row

definitions.meaning: a shack is a crude, roughly built dwelling
a row here is a noisy brawl or rowdy fight

explanation.definitionFit: A rough house is a crude hut, while roughhouse also means boisterous brawling, so both senses fit.

clue.text: True focal point of Surrealism

indicators.note: the focal point of a word is taken as its central letters

explanation.surface: A remark that genuine truth is the centre of the Surrealist movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'focal point of' takes the middle four letters of SURREALISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Real and true both mean genuine, not imaginary.

clue.text: Being inexperienced, I turned awkwardly

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters of the two words are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: A novice confesses to having turned round clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges I TURNED; 'Being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untested in a role has no experience of it.

clue.text: It's hard to resign, perhaps, after tough bargaining

indicators.note: perhaps hints the three words are one possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: After tough negotiations someone finds it hard to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals an anagram of HARD TO RESIGN; 'It's' and 'after' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd, hard-nosed haggling is named after the dealing of horse dealers.

clue.text: Archetype of one drink not written about

indicators.note: about tells us the word for not written goes around the others

parts.note: oral means spoken, not written
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: The prototype of a cocktail was never written down.
explanation.walkthrough: ORAL (not written) goes 'about' I (one) and GIN (drink).
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the first model or prototype from which copies are made.

clue.text: Gregarious in the get-together

explanation.definitionFit: A sociable person enjoys company, and a church or club party is called by the same word.

clue.text: Group to plug in speech

indicators.note: in speech tells us the word for plug is heard spoken, not written

parts.note: to plug a hole is to block it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to promote a group by giving it a plug in a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' signals a homophone: BLOCK (plug) sounds like BLOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of nations or parties acting together.

clue.text: A gumboil burst, getting rid of one complaint

indicators.note: burst means the letters of the phrase are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An abscess on the gum bursts and one ailment is cured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting rid of' removes I (one) from A GUMBOIL, and 'burst' rearranges the remaining AGUMBOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is lower back pain, a medical complaint or ailment.

clue.text: Sweet are the outskirts of the city on the literary river

parts.words: are the outskirts of the city
parts.note: C and Y are the first and last letters of the word city, so the phrase spells out those letters joined by and
the Floss is the river in George Eliot's novel The Mill on the Floss

explanation.surface: A sweet treat is sold on the edge of town by a river famous in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first piece as a statement: 'C and Y are the outskirts of the city', the first and last letters of 'city'. The Floss is from George Eliot's The Mill on the Floss.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun sugar on a stick, sold at fairs, is a confection or sweet.

clue.text: Clara, Pete and I may present a reredos

indicators.note: the three names may present, in a new order, the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: Three people, Clara, Pete and the speaker, might donate a church screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may present' signals an anagram of CLARA, PETE and I together; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is the ornamental screen behind a church altar, a kind of altar decoration.

clue.text: A sign the submariner gives on return

indicators.note: on return tells us the submariner's name is read backwards

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: A submarine crewman gives a signal as he comes back to port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' reverses NEMO, Jules Verne's submarine captain.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent or sign of things to come.

clue.text: They may cause sickness in game

definitions.meaning: a ship's pitching and tossing in rough seas makes people seasick
a gambling game of throwing coins at a mark

explanation.definitionFit: A boat's rolling motions bring on seasickness, and the phrase also names an old coin-throwing gambling game.

clue.text: Pleasant city

definitions.meaning: the French Riviera city on the Mediterranean

explanation.definitionFit: Nice means agreeable, and Nice is a resort city on the French Riviera.

clue.text: Non-existent, like some numbers

definitions.meaning: not real, existing only in the mind
in mathematics, multiples of the square root of minus one

explanation.definitionFit: Something unreal exists only in the mind, and mathematicians call multiples of the square root of minus one by this term.

clue.text: Blunter expletive? Nonsense

parts.note: balder means more plain or blunt, as in a bald statement
dash is a mild oath, as in dash it all

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a franker oath would help, then dismisses it as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: BALDER is 'blunter', as a bald statement is blunt; DASH! is a mild oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is senseless talk, rubbish or twaddle.

clue.text: Tree feller, commonly, was once a local worthy

parts.note: the alder is a tree of damp ground
feller is a colloquial form of fellow, and a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Someone who cut down trees was once an important person in the community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' suggests a woodcutter beside 'Tree', but it is the colloquial fellow, a man. 'was once' notes that aldermen no longer sit on English councils.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman was a senior elected member of a borough or county council, a civic dignitary.

clue.text: Fish train?

definitions.meaning: a shoal of fish swimming together
to train is to teach or discipline

explanation.definitionFit: A shoal of fish is called this, and as a verb it means to educate or discipline.

clue.text: It's a long story about the same outbreak

indicators.note: about tells us the long story goes around the word for the same

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem or tale
idem is Latin for the same

explanation.surface: A long tale about the same outbreak of disease is told again.
explanation.walkthrough: EPIC (a long story) goes 'about' IDEM, Latin for 'the same'.
explanation.definitionFit: A widespread outbreak of an infectious disease is an epidemic.

clue.text: Resolve to dump El Campeador in the river

indicators.note: in places the hero's name inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
El Campeador, the Champion, was the title of El Cid, the Castilian hero

explanation.surface: A decision to throw the Spanish hero's body into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: El Campeador ('the Champion') was the title of El Cid, the medieval Castilian hero; the Dee is a British river. 'to dump' only colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve is to make up your mind or settle a question.

clue.text: Accountant's revolutionary fall -

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant, with the possessive giving S
Jack Cade led the 1450 rebellion in Kent

explanation.surface: An accountant's dramatic downfall from radical ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is chartered accountant; Jack Cade led a revolt against Henry VI in 1450.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, water falling in stages.

clue.text: A smug sign in places swarming with workers

parts.note: pi is slang for sanctimonious or smug, short for pious
Aries the ram is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied sign hangs in a busy workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is British slang for sanctimonious. 'workers' are worker bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Hives full of worker bees are kept in bee yards, and the workers are the bees.

clue.text: List indicates a difficult tie in the semi, perhaps? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: difficult hints that the letters of the words are knotted up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A list shows a tough match is coming in the semi-final.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a tough semi-final; 'Quite the opposite' turns it round so the semi sits in the tie, which leaves the same letters for 'difficult' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set out item by item, to list.

clue.text: One looking hard for the Sun King?

parts.note: the Sun is a star
ER is the abbreviation for Rex or Regina, a monarch, as in Edward Rex

explanation.surface: A question whether someone staring intently is searching for Louis XIV, the Sun King.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Sun King' suggests Louis XIV of France, but it splits in two: our sun is a star, and a king is abbreviated from Latin Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gazes fixedly at another is staring, so a gazer is one who stares.

clue.text: Instrument introducing unfinished composition reverberated

indicators.note: the instrument is introducing, or taking inside it, the shortened composition

parts.note: a reed is a wind instrument, or a reed pipe

indicators.note: unfinished means the composition loses its last letter

parts.note: a sonata is a musical composition

explanation.surface: A musical instrument starts an incomplete piece, and the sound echoes.
explanation.walkthrough: A reed is a wind instrument, or the vibrating part of one; 'introducing' means the instrument takes the shortened piece inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that resonated echoed and rang on with sound.

clue.text: Conference for slimmers?

definitions.meaning: a restricted eating regime followed by those losing weight

explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a legislative assembly, as in Japan, and also a weight-loss eating plan.

clue.text: 20 inmates in a saintly 16

definitions.meaning: the residents of apiaries, from 20 across
A school in Cumbria, the school of 16 across

explanation.definitionFit: Honey insects live in hives, and St Bees is a well-known English public school in Cumbria.

clue.text: A mother and father of mankind

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: A mother and a father together began the whole human race.
explanation.walkthrough: DAM is a female parent of livestock; the first man of Genesis is the father of mankind.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man created is the ancestor of all humanity.

clue.text: Silk thread work replaced by stripe as basis for jumpers

parts.note: tram is a doubled silk thread used for the weft of fine fabrics

indicators.note: replaced is read as placed back, so the word for work runs backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a line is a stripe or band

explanation.surface: A piece of silk embroidery is swapped for a striped design as the base for knitted sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' suggests sweaters, but they are people who bounce. 'replaced', read as placed back, reverses OP to PO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprung canvas sheet is what gymnasts and children bounce on, the base for their leaps.

clue.text: Man had included note to attend

indicators.note: included tells us the note goes inside the contraction for man had

parts.note: he'd is the contraction of he had, a man having
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A man had added a reminder to be present.
explanation.walkthrough: HE'D (man had) takes in the note E.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to pay attention to or take notice of.

clue.text: They cheat, taking rest wrongly after spells at the helm

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters behind the spells at the helm

parts.note: a trick is a sailor's spell of duty at the wheel

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of rest are set in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Cheats take time off improperly after stints steering the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A TRICK is a turn at the helm in nautical slang; 'wrongly' rearranges REST to TERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Swindlers and hoaxers deceive people, playing tricks on them.
